goal:
This project folder is empty. Build a small command-line tool in it from scratch.

Write a Python program `wordfreq.py` that takes a path to a text file as its only argument and prints the ten most frequent words, one per line, as 'word count', most frequent first. Words are case-insensitive and punctuation is not part of a word. Ties break alphabetically so the output is deterministic.

It must handle a missing argument and an unreadable file by printing a clear message and exiting non-zero, rather than raising a traceback.

Also write `test_wordfreq.py`: a plain Python script (no pytest) that creates its own temporary input files, checks the ordering, the tie-breaking, the case-insensitivity, and both error paths, prints one 'OK:' line per check, and exits 0 only if every check passed.

Verify by running: python test_wordfreq.py. Report the exit code you actually saw. Delete any scratch files you create along the way.
